 Palace proving too easy to breach published at 17:15 GMT 17:15 GMT 
 Tottenham v Crystal Palace (17:30 GMT) 
 Tottenham away used to be a trip of trepidation across London for Crystal Palace fans but the tide has certainly turned in recent years.
 After nine straight top-flight losses at Spurs they have won on their last two visits, with their 3-1 victory in March particularly impressive.
 However, this is a Palace team in a very different spot. Defeat to Newcastle on Sunday was their fifth in just eight league matches under new boss Pierre Sage.
 They sit 17th having conceded a top-flight high of 19 goals in eight matches, the second most they have let in at this stage of a top-flight season after 22 in 1980-81.
 Of the 24 previous Premier League teams to concede 19 after eight games, 14 went on to be relegated. And another concerning stat is that they have let in at least two goals in 12 of their last 14 top-flight games.
 These defensive frailties, though, can't all be put at Sage's feet as they predate the Frenchman's summer arrival. Their tally of conceding 50 goals in 2026 is not only a Premier League high, but it's also six more than they conceded in the whole of 2025 and they still have 10 league matches to play this year.

 On whether he would play Lisandro Martinez again...
 No, I wouldn't, only because he looks like he has already gone. 
 His head isn't right. He is not going to be there long term, that is evident.
 You have to put the club first. Michael has got to make some big decisions. You can't have a liability in your team.
 People talked about Romero for years, and it is turning into that a little bit. That petulance, that behaviour on the pitch is not acceptable.
 He has been poor for a while and he has had injury problems. He is not the answer.

 'Amount of bodies on the line today was incredible' published at 17:12 GMT 17:12 GMT 
 FT: Man City 0-1 Brighton 
 Brighton & Hove Albion 
 Brighton goalkeeper Bart Verbruggen speaking to Sky Sports: "Unbelievable feeling. We go 1-0 up and then to hang tight the last 30-40 minutes we completely lost control of the game. The manager said this morning we have to dig deep and that's what we did. So happy to get over the line and can't wait to celebrate with the boys."
 On if Brighton are in the title race: "We are on game nine so not really. We'll take it game by game. See what happens because we have loads of games. Just focussing every day on what's ahead of us and the job we have. We will continue to do that and see where it leaves us at the end of the season. We are happy with the way we are playing - not just the results but the way we are playing too. We have to continue to develop that style and ruthlessness and we can do great things."
 On keeping a clean sheet: "Hard to point out one thing, the mentality to keep the ball out of the net - how hard we work. The amount of bodies put on the line today is incredible and credit to all the boys and staff and how hard we worked to keep the clean sheets. Hopefully we can get many more."
 On if this was one of his best personal performances: "I don't know - it was a good game from all of us. Happy to help the team and make some important saves but I wasn't the only one. I think there were four or five shots blocked in an amazing way as well. Joint effort from everyone. We celebrate and go again."

 Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Igor Thiago, who scored 27 goals last season for club and country, netted for just the second time in the Premier League this season
 By Jonty Colman BBC Sport journalist Igor Thiago continued his return to form as his second-half strike helped Brentford end their five-game wait for a win against Nottingham Forest. 
 The Bees had taken the lead on the half-hour mark when Nikola Milenkovic inadvertently steered past his own goalkeeper.
 Thiago, converted Brentford's second in the final 15 minutes for his second goal in three days - after finding the net at Sunderland in the Carabao Cup - and only his second in the Premier League this season. 
 His goal, in the 76th minute, was also the game's first shot on target.
 In a tense affair, with defeat leaving Forest 19th in the Premier League table, Brentford winger Dango Ouattara's moment of magic broke the deadlock.
 The Burkina Faso international skipped past Forest defender Murillo on the right wing before drilling a cross into the six-yard box.
 In his attemps to divert the ball, Milenkovic's block looped over his own goalkeeper Matz Sels and into the net. 
 Brentford captain Mathias Jensen nearly added the game's second before half-time with a free-kick that hit the crossbar.
 Visitors Forest had significantly more shots than the hosts but never looked likely to beat home goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher.
 Their best chance came early in the second half when substitute Ryan Yates headed over from close range. 
 But Thiago sealed three points for the hosts with his fourth goal of the campaign in all competitions. 
 Winger Jaidon Anthony started a counter-attack, moments after coming on as a substitute, before squaring the ball to Thiago whose shot did enough to beat Sels.
 Three points for Keith Andrews' Brentford moves them up to sixth.
 Brentford analysis: Thiago rediscovers scoring touch 
 Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Igor Thiago is joint-fourth, alongside teammate Kevin Schade, on Brentford's all-time Premier League goalscorer's list
 Only Manchester City's Erling Haaland (27) netted more Premier League goals than Thiago's 22 last season. But this season, it has been a different story.
 Until four days ago, Thiago had scored just twice in 10 matches in all competitions, one of which was against Championship side Birmingham City in an EFL Cup second-round drubbing.
 But, after scoring as a substitute on Wednesday at Sunderland, again in the EFL Cup, the Brazil forward now has four goals in all competitions from 12 outings and with two in three days, showed a huge sigh of relief after sealing victory for the Bees.
 "It means a lot to me. I was waiting for this goal for so long this season," Thiago, whose only other league goal came at home to Chelsea, told Premier League Productions.
 "Thank you Lord, to score one more goal at home. I am really happy."
 In the summer, Thiago went to the World Cup with Brazil. But, after starting in their opening match against Morocco, he was an unused substitute for the remainder of the campaign.
 With back-to-back goals, his form will only complement a Brentford side who despite missing Thiago's goals from last season, are showing early season signs of being in the European mix.
 Nottingham Forest analysis: Is Glasner under pressure? 
 Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Oliver Glasner arrived at the City Ground in the summer, replacing Vitor Pereira
 More dropped points for Forest leaves them second-bottom before a meeting with league leaders Manchester City next weekend.
 Forest have just one Premier League win in nine games since the arrival of Oliver Glasner as head coach in the summer and have picked up a single point from the last 15 available will raise some eyebrows.
 Only Manchester United (18.6) have managed more shots per game in the Premier League this season than Forest (16.9), but they are the division's lowest scorers.
 In nine games, they have mustered just six goals. Five of those matches saw them fail to score.
 With a further 15 shots at Brentford, and just one on target coming in the 78th minute from James McAtee, their failure to convert attempts into goals could prove costly for both their chances of success this season and Glasner's hopes of staying on as head coach.
